title: VPC operator semaphore leak causing Helm apply timeouts and tenant-scoped rollback guard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers reported failed on-prem upgrades where the VPC/operator reconcile loop exhausted goroutine-level semaphores causing Helm release apply operations to stall and time out. Customers observed partial CR state (finalizers present, secrets not rotated) and subsequent config drift that blocked automated rollups. This ticket tracks the investigation, hotfix implementation, and coordinated customer rollouts and runbook updates.
timeline: 2026-03-03 - Customer A IR opened after scheduled maintenance window: helm apply timed out; nodeagent not updated; ticket routed to onprem support.
2026-03-04 - Customer B opened similar escalation; symptoms matched: controller log shows repeated 'acquire semaphore' warnings and long queue lengths prior to helm timeout.
2026-03-05 - Local repro created in staging using a synthetic tenant with heavy concurrent upgrades; reproduced semaphore exhaustion and stalled reconcile workers.

2026-03-06 - Root-cause hypothesis: unbounded concurrent reconcile paths in v2 operator combined with a new async webhook path leaked semaphore tokens on certain error paths (context cancellation + deferred unlock missed).
2026-03-07 - Engineering spike: wrote minimal patch to add metrics and defensive unlocks; confirmed immediate improvement in staging under load.

2026-03-09 - Decided to ship a conservative hotfix that (1) caps concurrent reconcile tokens per-operator, (2) adds a tenant-scoped rollback guard that avoids destructive finalizer removal, and (3) exposes a repair endpoint to safely replay Helm applies for stuck tenants.

2026-03-11 - Draft PR created (github.com/redwood/operator/pull/4293); initial QA pass passed smoke tests but uncovered an edge case in the KVCACHE migration path that required an additional safe-check.
2026-03-12 - Emergency customer call: applied manual remediation (requeue + secret reapplier) for Customer A to restore during their maintenance window.
2026-03-14 - Hotfix candidate operator-3.14.2-hotfix1 built and validated in canary cluster. Preparing staged rollout and runbook publication.
remediation_steps: Hotfix code changes: add per-operator semaphore cap with defensive unlocks in all error/ctx-cancel paths.
Introduce tenant-scoped rollback guard: when a helm apply fails mid-flight, mark release with 'stuck-reconcile' annotation instead of forcibly removing finalizers; allow manual/automated repair.
Add a 'repair-apply' controller endpoint that replays the last successful Helm manifest with a dry-run validation before applying changes.
Backfill migration script to detect CRs with mismatched finalizer/secret states and requeue them safely.
Publish a manual remediation runbook and step-by-step playbook for SEs that includes log queries, requeue commands, and a safe secret reapply script.
Coordinate with affected customers to run remediation during their approved maintenance windows.
Post-release: run tenant audit to detect any remaining partial states and remediate automatically where safe.
testing_plan: Unit tests for semaphore unlocks across all reconcile code paths (including ctx cancel and webhook errors).
Load test: synthetic 250 concurrent tenant upgrades in staging to validate no starvation and no Helm timeouts.
Integration test: simulate secret rotation mid-upgrade to ensure tenant-scoped rollback guard preserves finalizers and allows repair endpoint to succeed.
Chaos test: randomly inject reconcile panics and ensure operator recovers and requeues without leaking tokens.
E2E customer scenario: reproduce Customer B's exact manifest and run the full upgrade in a private staging tenant.
Security review: confirm repair endpoint requires tenant-scoped RBAC and audit logging enabled before release.
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy operator-3.14.2-hotfix1 to our internal canary cluster and one low-risk customer cluster (Customer C) for 24h.
Phase 1: roll to 5% of onprem tenants (region-by-region) with SEs on-call and run automated tenant audits every 1h.
Phase 2: expand to customers with maintenance windows scheduled over next 48h (coordinated with Support).
Full: roll to remaining onprem clusters after 72h of canary verification.

Rollback criteria: if Helm apply failure rate for targeted tenants increases by >2x or any customer reports loss of finalizers/data, initiate operator downgrade to previous patch and follow the rollback runbook.
Communication: notify customers in advance via incident channel; update status page during rollout steps.
verification_criteria: No new semaphore-exhaustion warnings in controller logs for canary region after 24h.
Helm apply timeout rate reduced to baseline (<=0.1% per-upgrade) across canary tenants.
Automated repair endpoint succeeds for 10/10 previously stuck CR samples in staging.
Support runbook verified by SEs on at least 2 onprem remediation exercises without needing code changes.
No increase in customer reported incidents during Phase 1 compared to baseline.
postmortem_actions: 1) Schedule an ops retrospective with Support and SEs to review customer communication and remediation timelines.
2) Add operator integration test that runs synthetic concurrent upgrades nightly to catch semaphore regressions.
3) Update onprem upgrade preflight to include semaphore/token health checks and fail fast with clear remediation steps.
4) Ship documentation update to Console and Support KB for the new repair endpoint and tenant-scoped rollback behavior.
5) Track follow-up tickets for any improvements discovered during rollout (e.g., granular per-tenant semaphore quotas).
